picks.title: Reservoir Fires Off Infringement and DMCA Suits Against Suno and Anthropic, Demanding Nearly $340 Million
picks.rationale: New filings: independent publisher Reservoir has brought two separate infringement and DMCA suits against Suno and Anthropic, seeking close to $340M. It is the first time one rights holder has sued a music generator and a general LLM maker together, which matters to anyone shipping AI-assisted tracks.
picks.excerpt: Reservoir is seeking hundreds of millions of dollars in damages from Anthropic and Suno in a pair of new copyright infringement suits.

picks.title: Universal Music Group & AI Gaming Company TYGER Announce Licensing Deal
picks.rationale: A new licensing deal: UMG is the first major label to license TYGER, an AI game platform that adapts licensed songs to gameplay in real time. It opens a new licensed channel for adaptive and interactive music.
picks.excerpt: UMG becomes the first major to license TYGER, an AI gaming platform that adapts licensed songs to gameplay in real time.

picks.title: Agentic Music Post-Production (MixAgent)
picks.rationale: A new research release: MixAgent is an agent pipeline that mirrors how an audio engineer works. It groups the tracks, then builds an interpretable and editable mixing plan guided by a reference song. This is the tools card of the set and the most directly actionable for producers.
picks.excerpt: MixAgent is an agentic pipeline for music post-production that follows audio engineers' workflow: grouping and planning agents build interpretable, editable mixing plans guided by a reference song.

picks.title: Fontaines DC Blindsided by Unsanctioned, 'Ironic' Use of AI on 'Marianne' Music Video
picks.rationale: A new incident: AI was used on Fontaines D.C.'s 'Marianne' video without the band's approval. It is a concrete case of creative control and consent breaking down in music-video production, separate from the 10-22 Gavras copycat story.
picks.excerpt: Fontaines D.C. found themselves in a darkly ironic AI scandal after they found out someone used the tech on one of their music videos.

picks.title: Claude's lyrics are diluting real lyrics, say music publishers in latest Anthropic proceedings
picks.rationale: A new court hearing on fair use in UMG/Concord/ABKCO v Anthropic. The publishers argued that AI-generated lyrics dilute the market for real ones, a market-harm theory that could shape how AI training on lyrics is judged. The Concord v Anthropic case has not been covered in the 30-day history.
picks.excerpt: The big debate over whether or not AI training is fair use under US copyright law was taking place in court again yesterday, this time in the context of music, specifically lyrics, with the copyright legal battle between AI company Anthropic and the Universal, Concord and ABKCO music publishers
